pack.title: Noise & parties
pack.description: Bass through the wall at midnight. Firm, neighborly, documented.

scenarios.setting: Midnight. You knock; your neighbor opens with the music behind them.
scenarios.jab: Oh come on, it's Saturday. Loosen up.

replies.line: Enjoy Saturday. Turn it down by one.
replies.why: Permission plus a small specific ask is easier to grant than a lecture to endure.
It asks for almost nothing, which makes refusing it almost impossible.

replies.line: Sounds like a great night — I just need the bass down a hair.
replies.why: Joining the fun verbally while asking technically keeps you allies, not enemies.

replies.line: Your playlist slaps. My ceiling disagrees. Meet halfway?
replies.why: Complimenting the music while citing the ceiling splits the difference with a grin.

replies.line: I'm the fun neighbor. After quiet hours.
replies.why: It claims the fun title on your schedule, which splits the difference cleanly.

trap.line: Turn it off or I'm calling the cops.
trap.why: Opening with the nuclear threat spends your only leverage on night one.

scenarios.setting: Morning after. Your neighbor, taking out trash, spots you.

replies.line: Grandpa needs his sleep. Thanks for last night.
replies.why: Taking the nickname while thanking him banks goodwill for next time.
It declines the rematch and keeps the hallway peace in three words.

replies.line: Haha — worth it though, hope it was a good one.
replies.why: Grace about your own complaint makes the next one land softer.
Owning the nickname with a fake tariff ends the bit as friends.
It denies the damage with a grin, which banks the goodwill anyway.
